# @ratmath/numtheory 0.3.0: full documentation

> Number theory for RatMath: primes with certificates, congruences, Diophantine equations, p-adic numbers, elliptic curves, number fields with proven class groups and units, and zeta and L values. From https://ratmath.com/numtheory/, commit d8bf4a5. Each page ends with a runnable example; in it, PRINT(...) prints.


---

Page: https://ratmath.com/numtheory/index.html

@ratmath/numtheory

## Number theory with proofs attached

From a first course to algebraic number theory: primes that come with a certificate, congruences and reciprocity, Diophantine equations, p-adic numbers, elliptic curves, and the arithmetic of number fields.

### What is here

Every phase of the plan is built: primes with certificates, factoring, arithmetic functions, congruences, reciprocity and sums of squares; linear and Pell equations, continued fractions and binary quadratic forms; p-adic numbers; elliptic curves over the rationals and over finite fields, with the factoring method and the primality certificates built on them; rings of integers of number fields, prime ideals, class groups and unit groups; and the analytic side, with exact prime counts, Dirichlet characters, and values of zeta and L functions.

### A first program

```js
import { isPrime, provePrime, verifyCertificate, factor, formatFactors, jacobiSteps, twoSquaresAll, pellSolutions, classGroup, padic, ellipticCurve } from "@ratmath/numtheory";

isPrime(2n ** 61n - 1n);                     // true, proven: Baillie–PSW has no exceptions below 2^64
const r = provePrime(2n ** 127n - 1n);       // a Pocklington certificate, a tree of smaller primes
verifyCertificate(r.certificate);            // { valid: true }, by a checker that shares no code with the search
formatFactors(factor(2n ** 64n + 1n));       // "274177 · 67280421310721"

jacobiSteps(1001, 9907).value;               // -1, with every reciprocity step written out
twoSquaresAll(325);                          // [[18n, 1n], [17n, 6n], [15n, 10n]]
pellSolutions(2, 7).solutions(4);            // [[3n, 1n], [5n, 3n], [13n, 9n], [27n, 19n]]
classGroup(-3299).structure;                 // [3n, 9n]: the class group is C3 × C9
padic(-1, 5n).sqrt().toString(12);           // "…223032431212": i in the 5-adic integers

formatFactors(factor(2n ** 128n + 1n));      // "59649589127497217 · 5704689200685129054721", by the elliptic curve method
isPrime(10n ** 60n + 7n);                    // true: an elliptic curve certificate, checked by the same verifier
ellipticCurve([-43, 166]).torsion().structure;   // [7]: y² = x³ − 43x + 166 has a rational point of order 7

ringOfIntegers([-8n, -2n, -1n, 1n]).describePrime(2).primes.length;   // 3: in Dedekind's cubic, 2 splits completely
String(idealClassGroup([-65n, 0n, 0n, 1n]));  // "class group of Q(α), α a root of x³ − 65: C3 × C6, h = 18", proven
unitGroup([-2n, 0n, 0n, 1n]).fundamentalUnits;   // [1 + α + α²]: the fundamental unit of Q(∛2), proven fundamental
primePi(10n ** 12n);                         // 37607912018n, by Meissel's formula
zetaValue(3).compactedDecimalInterval();     // "1.202056903159594285[38:41]": an interval that contains ζ(3)
lValueExact(kroneckerCharacter(-23), 0);     // 3: the class number of Q(√−23), as an L-value
```

### Four ideas

A proof, or a refusal. "Prime" means proven: below 2⁶⁴ by a test known to have no exceptions there, above it by a certificate (from the factors of n − 1, or from an elliptic curve) that an independent verifier checks. When no certificate can be found, `isPrime` refuses and says why, rather than guessing. A composite comes with a factor or a witness. See [Primes and certificates](https://ratmath.com/numtheory/primes.html).

Every "no" has a reason. A congruence with no solution names the gcd that blocks it, a number that is not a sum of two squares names the prime, two forms that are not equivalent name their different reduced forms, and an equivalence comes with the matrix that proves it.

Certified without hypotheses. Class groups and unit groups are usually computed fast under the generalised Riemann hypothesis and checked separately, if at all. Here the check is part of the answer: Minkowski's bound for the generators, and a saturation argument with a proven lower bound on regulators for the relations. Values of zeta and L functions come as intervals with rational endpoints. See [Class groups](https://ratmath.com/numtheory/class-groups.html) and [Zeta and L values](https://ratmath.com/numtheory/l-values.html).

Exact at any size, lazily where it must be. Everything is BigInt and Core Rational arithmetic. p-adic numbers have infinitely many digits, so they are rules that compute as many as asked, exactly; what digits alone cannot decide, such as whether a number is exactly zero, is reported as unknown. See [p-adic numbers](https://ratmath.com/numtheory/padic.html).

### The plan, completed

From the [library roadmap](https://github.com/ratmath/ratmath/blob/main/docs/design/library-roadmap.md#4-a-number-theory-package-ratmathnumtheory).

| Phase | Contents | |

| 1 | Primes with certificates, arithmetic functions, congruences, reciprocity, sums of squares, re-exports | built |

| 2 | Diophantine equations and binary quadratic forms | built |

| 3 | p-adic numbers | built |

| 4 | Elliptic curves; ECM and curve-based certificates | built |

| 5 | Integral bases, discriminants, prime ideal factorisation | built |

| 6 | Class groups and unit groups | built |

| 7 | π(x), characters, ζ and L values | built |

It builds on Core and algebraic (the modular kernel and the algebraic numbers that continued fractions expand); continued fractions, Pell's equation and the Chinese remainder theorem moved here from algebraic.

### Try it

```js
// primes, proofs and a little of everything
const p = provePrime(2n ** 107n - 1n);
PRINT("2^107 − 1:", p.certificate.kind, verifyCertificate(p.certificate));
PRINT("F₆ =", formatFactors(factor(2n ** 64n + 1n)));
PRINT("1105 as two squares:", twoSquaresAll(1105).map(([a, b]) => `${a}² + ${b}²`).join(", "));
PRINT("x² − 2y² = 7:", pellSolutions(2, 7).solutions(5));
PRINT("h(−3299) =", classNumber(-3299), "structure", classGroup(-3299).structure);
PRINT("Q(∛65):", String(idealClassGroup([-65n, 0n, 0n, 1n])));
PRINT("π(10¹⁰) =", primePi(10n ** 10n), "  ζ(3) ∈", zetaValue(3).compactedDecimalInterval());
padic("1/3", 5n).toString(16)
```

Page: https://ratmath.com/numtheory/reference.html

Reference

## Everything in the library

Every export of `@ratmath/numtheory`. Whole-number arguments may be numbers, `BigInt`s, digit strings or Core `Rational`s with denominator 1; a JavaScript number that is not whole is refused. Results are `BigInt`s, except symbols (−1, 0, 1) and valuations, which are plain numbers. Refusals throw a `NumberTheoryError` whose `code` says why.

### Primes and certificates

| Export | What it does |

| primes(limit) | The primes up to the limit (at most 10⁷), by the sieve of Eratosthenes. |

| primePi(x), nthPrime(k) | π(x) exactly, up to 10¹² (a sieve below 10⁷, Meissel's formula above); the k-th prime. |

| isPrime(n) | Proven below 2⁶⁴ (Baillie–PSW); above, by a certificate, or throws "unproven". |

| isProbablePrime(n) | Baillie–PSW alone: fast, not a proof above 2⁶⁴. |

| nextPrime(n), prevPrime(n), primesBetween(a, b) | Neighbouring primes; the primes in a window (segmented sieve, b
| Export | What it does |

| factor(n, { prove, effort }) | [{ prime, exponent, proven }], increasing: trial division, Pollard rho, p − 1, then the elliptic curve method. Refuses with "too-hard" when the factors are out of reach; effort scales the number of curves. |

| ecm(n, { B1, B2, curves, sigma, details }) | The elliptic curve method: a proper factor or null; with details, { factor, stage, sigma, B1, B2 }. |

| ecmCurve(n, sigma, { B1, B2 }) | One Suyama curve, as a report. |

| formatFactors(fs) | "2^3 · 3 · 5^2". |

| trialDivide(n, limit) | { found: Map(prime → exponent), rest }. |

| pollardRho(n, { steps, seed }) | A nontrivial factor by Brent's rho, or null. |

| pollardPm1(n, bound) | A factor p with p − 1 smooth to the bound, or null. |

| factorInteger, modPow, modInverse, multiplicativeOrder, primitiveRoot, discreteLogMod, sqrtMod, lll, recognize | Re-exported from @ratmath/algebraic, which keeps the modular kernel for its finite fields. |

### Arithmetic functions

| Export | What it does |

| divisors(n) | The positive divisors, increasing. |

| sigma(n, k), tau(n) | σk​(n)=∑d∣n​dk (k = 1 by default); the number of divisors. |

| totient(n), jordan(n, k), carmichael(n) | Euler's φ, Jordan's Jk​, Carmichael's λ. |

| mobius(n), liouville(n) | μ(n) and λ(n)=(−1)Ω(n). |

| omega(n), bigOmega(n), radical(n), isSquarefree(n) | Distinct primes, primes with multiplicity, their product, square-freeness. |

| aliquotSum(n), classify(n), isPerfect(n) | s(n)=σ(n)−n; "perfect", "abundant" or "deficient". |

| aliquotSequence(n, { steps, max }) | { terms, ending }: "terminates", "perfect", "amicable", "cycle of length k" or "unfinished". |

| amicablePairs(limit), perfectNumbers(count), lucasLehmer(p) | Amicable pairs up to the limit; even perfect numbers; the Lucas–Lehmer test of 2ᵖ − 1. |

| dirichlet(f, g), mobiusInversion(F) | Dirichlet convolution; f=F∗μ. |

| unit, one, id | ε, the constant 1, the identity: building blocks for convolutions. |

| isMultiplicative(f, limit) | Checks f(mn)=f(m)f(n) on coprime pairs up to the limit (a check, not a proof). |

### Congruences

| Export | What it does |

| solveLinear(a, b, m) | Every x mod m with ax≡b: { solutions, modulus, g, reduced }, or no solutions with the reason. |

| crt(residues, moduli) | The Chinese remainder theorem for any moduli: { x, modulus } or null. |

| solveLinearSystem([[a, b, m], …]) | Each ai​x≡bi​(modmi​) reduced, then combined. |

| polyMod(poly, x, m) | An integer polynomial (constant first) at x, mod m. |

| hensel(poly, r, p, k) | Lifts a simple root mod p to the root mod pk. |

| rootsMod(poly, m) | Every root mod m: prime powers by lifting, combined by CRT. |

| hasPrimitiveRoot(n), primitiveRootMod(n), order(a, n) | Gauss's condition; the least primitive root or null; the multiplicative order. |

| discreteLog(g, h, n) | The least x with gx≡h, or null (baby-step giant-step). |

| valuation(n, p) | vp​(n); Infinity for 0. |

| factorialValuation(n, b) | The exponent of b in n!: Legendre's formula ∑k​⌊n/pk⌋ for a prime; the largest k with bk∣n! for any b≥2 (trailing zeros in base b). A BigInt when too large for a plain number. |

### Reciprocity

| Export | What it does |

| legendre(a, p), jacobi(a, n), kronecker(a, n) | The quadratic symbols, as −1, 0 or 1. |

| jacobiSteps(a, n) | { value, steps }: the reciprocity computation, one line per step. |

| eulerCriterion(a, p), gaussLemma(a, p) | { power, value }; { value, mu, large }. |

| quadraticResidues(n), sqrtsMod(a, n) | The squares mod n; every square root of a mod n. |

### Sums of squares

| Export | What it does |

| primeAsTwoSquares(p) | p ≡ 1 (mod 4) as a2+b2, by Euclid's algorithm on p and a square root of −1 (Brillhart). |

| twoSquaresAll(n), twoSquares(n), twoSquaresReason(n) | Every a2+b2=n with a≥b≥0 (Gaussian integers); one; why or why not. |

| r2(n), r4(n), rk(n, k) | Representations counted with signs and order: Jacobi's formulas, and the theta series for any k ≤ 12. |

| threeSquares(n), fourSquares(n) | Three squares unless n=4a(8b+7) (then null); four always. |

| pythagoreanTriples(limit) | Primitive triples with c ≤ limit, by Euclid's formula. |

| triplesWithHypotenuse(c), triplesWithLeg(a) | Every triple, primitive or not, with that hypotenuse or leg. |

### Diophantine equations

| Export | What it does |

| linearDiophantine(coefficients, c) | { solvable, g, particular, basis }: every solution is the particular one plus an integer combination of the basis. |

| nonNegativeSolutions(a, b, c) | The solutions of ax + by = c in non-negative integers. |

| frobenius(coins), coinWays(amount, coins) | The largest unpayable amount; the number of ways to pay. |

| pellSolutions(D, N), normEquation(D, N) | x2−Dy2=N: { kind: "infinite", unit, fundamental, solutions(count) } or { kind: "finite", solutions }. |

| egyptianGreedy(q), egyptianShortest(q, options) | Distinct unit fractions: greedy, or a shortest expansion by search. |

### Continued fractions

| Export | What it does |

| continuedFraction(x, terms) | The terms of a rational or real algebraic number, exactly. |

| convergents(terms) | The convergents as Core Rationals. |

| fromContinuedFraction(terms, period) | The number [a₀; a₁, …] or [preperiod; period repeating], as an AlgebraicReal. |

| periodicContinuedFraction(x) | { preperiod, period } of a quadratic irrational. |

| pell(D), fundamentalUnit(d), fromQuadratic(p, q, d, r) | The least solution of x2−Dy2=±1; the fundamental unit of Q(d​); (p+qd​)/r as an AlgebraicReal. |

### Binary quadratic forms

| Export | What it does |

| form(a, b, c), new Form(a, b, c) | ax2+bxy+cy2: discriminant, at(x, y), transform(M), reduce() → { form, matrix }, cycle(), isReduced(), isPrimitive(). |

| equivalent(f, g) | { equivalent: true, matrix } with f ∘ matrix = g, or false with the reason. |

| compose(f, g), principalForm(D), inverseForm(f) | Gauss composition (reduced); the identity class; the inverse class. |

| reducedForms(D), classNumber(D) | One reduced form per class; h(D), the narrow one for D > 0. |

| classGroup(D) | { D, h, forms, identity, classOf, compose, inverse, order, structure }; structure lists the invariant factors. |

| representations(f, n), represent(f, n) | Every (x, y) with f(x, y) = n for definite f; one proper representation for any D, or null. |

### Elliptic curves

| Export | What it does |

| ellipticCurve([a, b]), ellipticCurve([a1, a2, a3, a4, a6]) | A curve over Q; with { mod: p }, over Fp​. An EllipticCurve, with a1 … a6, b2 … b8, c4, c6, discriminant, j, modulus, coefficients, infinity. |

| E.point(x, y), E.has(P), E.equal(P, Q) | A checked point { x, y }; membership; equality. |

| E.add(P, Q), E.sub(P, Q), E.neg(P), E.double(P), E.mul(k, P) | The group law. |

| E.order(P) | A BigInt; over Q, Infinity for a point of infinite order. |

| E.torsion() | Over Q: { order, structure, points, generators }. |

| E.shortModel(), E.minimalModel() | { curve, to(P), from(P), … }: a short integral model; the global minimal model with its change of variables u, r, s, t. |

| E.badPrimes(), E.reduction(p), E.conductor(), E.modulo(p) | Reduction: { prime, type, split, discriminantValuation, conductorExponent }; the conductor when no additive prime is 2 or 3; the curve over Fp​. |

| E.naiveHeight(P), E.height(P, { doublings }) | H(P); a proven enclosure { lower, upper, exact } of the canonical height. |

| E.rationalPoints(bound) | A search for points of small height. |

| E.count({ method, log }), E.trace() | Over Fp​: the number of points by "naive", "bsgs", "schoof" or "auto"; the trace of Frobenius. |

| E.points(), E.liftX(x), E.randomPoint(seed), E.structure() | All points (p ≤ 10⁶); the points above an x; a reproducible point; the group as Z/n1​×Z/n2​. |

| E.divisionPolynomial(n) | Coefficients of the n-th division polynomial of a short curve over Fp​. |

### p-adic numbers

| Export | What it does |

| padic(x, p) | A p-adic number from a whole number, fraction text, Rational or another p-adic. |

| Padic | approx(N), valuation(), norm(), digits(k), toString(k), mod(N), add, sub, mul, div, inv, pow, shift, sqrt, isSquare, exp, log, equalsTo(y, N). Lazy and exact; an undecidable valuation throws "unknown-valuation". |

| henselRoot(coefficients, r0, p) | The root of a polynomial starting at r0, by Newton's method. |

| teichmuller(a, p) | The (p − 1)-th root of unity ≡ a (mod p). |

| expansion(x, p) | { valuation, preperiod, period } of a rational's eventually periodic digits. |

| padicValuation(x, p), padicNorm(x, p) | vp​(x) and ∣x∣p​ of a rational. |

### Number fields

| Export | What it does |

| NumberField, NumberFieldElement | Re-exported from @ratmath/algebraic. Wherever a field is expected, the coefficients of an irreducible polynomial (constant first) work too. |

| ringOfIntegers(K) | The ring of integers, an Order, by the Round 2 algorithm; cached on the field. |

| Order | basis, discriminant, index, polyDiscriminant, signature, steps, traceMatrix, ramifiedPrimes, coordinates(x), element(coords), contains(x), primesAbove(p), describePrime(p), ideal(...generators), unitIdeal. |

| integralBasis(K), fieldDiscriminant(K), primeDecomposition(K, p) | Shortcuts for the basis, the discriminant and primesAbove. |

| PrimeIdeal | p, e, f, norm, generators, valuation(x) of an element, ideal or prime, toIdeal(), equals. |

| Ideal | A fractional ideal: norm, basis, minimum, isIntegral, isOne, isPrime, mul, add, div, pow, inverse, contains(x), equals, factor() as [{ prime, exponent }]. |

| idealClassGroup(K, options) | A ClassGroup: h, structure, generators, classOf(I), orderOf(I), isPrincipal(I) as { principal, generator }, proven, certificate, minkowskiBound, factorBase. Options certify, maxBound, maxIndexPrime, budget, rounds. |

| unitGroup(K, options) | A UnitGroup: rank, torsionOrder, rootOfUnity, fundamentalUnits, regulator, isUnit(x), exponents(u) as { torsion, exponents }, proven, certificate. |

| fieldClassNumber(K), regulator(K), minkowskiBound(K) | The class number, the regulator (a double), and the floor of Minkowski's bound. |

| formToIdeal(f, K) | The ideal aZ+2−b+D​​Z of the quadratic field of discriminant D for a form (a, b, c). |

### Counting primes, characters, zeta and L values

| Export | What it does |

| meissel(x) | { pi, y, a, phi, P2 }: π(x)=φ(x,a)+a−1−P2​ with a=π(3x​), for x ≤ 10¹². |

| legendrePhi(x, a) | How many n ≤ x have no prime factor among the first a primes. |

| dirichletCharacter(q, m) | The character χq​(m,⋅) in Conrey's numbering, a DirichletCharacter. |

| DirichletCharacter | modulus, number, order, conductor, isPrimitive, isPrincipal, isReal, isEven, parity, exponent(n) (the fraction t with χ(n)=e2πit, or null), value(n), at(n) for real characters, exponents(), primitive(), induce(modulus), mul, pow, conjugate, gaussSum(). |

| dirichletGroup(q) | { modulus, order, characters, principal, primitive, real, structure, orthogonality(a, b) }, for q ≤ 20000. |

| kroneckerCharacter(D) | The Kronecker symbol (D/⋅) as a character modulo \|D\|. |

| bernoulli(n), bernoulliPolynomial(n, x), generalizedBernoulli(k, χ) | Bn​ (with B1​=−1/2), Bn​(x), and Bk,χ​. |

| zetaExact(n) | A Rational for n ≤ 0; { coefficient, piPower } for even n > 0. |

| lValueExact(χ, n) | L(n,χ) for an integer n ≤ 0: a Rational for a real character, else an element of a cyclotomic field. |

| zetaValue(s, { bits }) | A proven enclosure of ζ(s): a RationalInterval for real s, { re, im } for [σ, t]. Width below 2−bits, 64 by default. |

| hurwitzZeta(s, a, { bits }) | An enclosure of ζ(s,a) for a rational a in (0, 1]. |

| lValue(χ, s, { bits }) | An enclosure of L(s,χ) anywhere in the plane (modulus ≤ 5000); at s = 1 for a non-principal character. |

### Integers and the rest

| Export | What it does |

| isqrt(n), iroot(n, k), gcd(a, b), lcm(a, b), egcd(a, b) | Integer roots, gcd and lcm, and Bézout's { g, x, y }. Any whole number in (number, BigInt, numeric string, Core Integer or whole Rational); BigInts out. |

| NumberTheoryError | Thrown for refusals; code is one of "bad-argument", "too-large", "too-hard", "unproven", "unknown-valuation", "not-a-square", "diverges", "singular", "not-on-curve", "budget", "pole", "precision", "unsupported". |

| plan | The phases still to come: empty, everything planned is built. |

### Try it

```js
// a tour: one call from each section
PRINT(provePrime(2n ** 89n - 1n).certificate.kind, formatFactors(factor(10n ** 18n + 1n)));
PRINT(sigma(28), totient(1001), crt([1, 2, 3], [5, 7, 9]));
PRINT(ellipticCurve([2, 3], { mod: 97 }).count(), ecm(2n ** 128n + 1n), ellipticCurve([0, 1]).torsion().structure);
PRINT(jacobi(1001, 9907), twoSquaresAll(65), fourSquares(2026));
PRINT(frobenius([6, 9, 20]), pellSolutions(2, 7).fundamental, classGroup(-3299).structure);
PRINT(fieldDiscriminant([-2n, 0n, 0n, 1n]), fieldClassNumber([-7n, 0n, 0n, 1n]), regulator([-2n, 0n, 0n, 1n]));
PRINT(primePi(10n ** 9n), String(dirichletCharacter(7, 3)), zetaExact(-3), String(zetaExact(4)));
padic(-1, 5n).sqrt().toString(16)
```
